newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes supported by futures, Oman trades +10.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes supported by futures, Oman trades +10.

text.p: Crude prices in Asia were supported on Monday by the rebound in crude futures prices on Friday but otherwise were mostly quiet.
Oman remained the focus of the Middle East market with two U.S. majors still actively making enquiries.

A European major sold 400,000 barrels of Oman on Friday at MPM +10 cents to a U.S. major. The U.S. company also took 100,000 barrels top up from a European trader at MPM + nine cents to make up a cargo.
The European major offered Oman at MPM +12 cents Monday but did not face any firm bids from the two majors seen as buyers.
The major is believed to hold most, if not all, the remaining December Oman cargoes.
Regional grades were also quiet. Most Indonesian grades were said to have been traded for November liftings.
In paper trading, Brent/Dubai was quoted for December at $2.25/$2.37 per barrel, compared with $2.23/$2.40 on Friday.
Brent spreads were mostly steady, but Dubai spreads were slightly weaker as players focused further forward onto January. Buying interest for Dubai wet cargoes was seen waning.
December/January was 40/48 cents from 43/48 and January/February was 45/51 from 45/50.
Crude oil futures were holding their bullish tone by late afternoon on Monday, continuing the retracement of last week's losses.
In London, December Brent was down one cent at $24.21 from Friday, but other contracts were firmer. January was up 14 cents at $23.60.
NYMEX December crude futures, were bid at $24.86, flat to the New York close on Friday.
